reply_text:
㊣ ("they reveal a separate problem") Agreed. If a fix that matches Lean breaks a row, the row was relying on a place where the port departs from Lean. When that happens, we won't hunt for the fix that broke it. We run the comparator cold on that row, and its first difference is the next thing to fix. That fits the fix-forward rule. I've added it to my wake checklist.

㊟ ("known correct due to the comparator") One limit: the comparator only checks the terms of the row the fix targeted. A fix can also change how other syntax is elaborated, and those changes are checked only when another row's comparator run reaches them. Running the comparator on the broken row catches both cases. If its difference is in code the fix changed, the fix itself needs another pass.
